events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to St. Joseph by boat.** It's the best of the four, rated about 2 (average).
- **Fish well out, around 100 to 120+ feet of water.** That's where the most recent St. Joseph boat reports say anglers were working.
- **Expect to run lines deep.** No fish depth was reported for St. Joseph in July, so I'd start deep and adjust.
- **Start with spoons.** The July reports from South Haven and the July 2022 reports from Grand Haven and Muskegon all mention spoons as the producer.
- **Skip the piers for now.** None of the four ports has a recent pier report, and the lake is warm.

Ratings for this week (0 slow to 4 excellent):

| Port | Rating | Confidence |
|---|---|---|
| St. Joseph | 2 (average) | Moderate |
| South Haven | 1 (below average) | Moderate |
| Grand Haven | 1 (below average) | Low |
| Muskegon | 1 (below average) | Low |

## Why

- **St. Joseph is the best bet:** the July 5 St. Joseph report rated boat fishing average, with anglers fishing past 120 feet, while South Haven's report that week was below average.
- **Expect deep water to matter:** the July 5 reports at South Haven and St. Joseph both put the fish well out, and I'd expect that to continue.
- **Spoons are the safe bet:** the July 5 South Haven report says most fish came on spoons.
- **Grand Haven and Muskegon are weaker:** their most recent boat reports are from June, and the similar-temperature weeks in past seasons were slow.

## Evidence

**Recent reports**
- St. Joseph, 2023-07-05: boat fishing was "decent," with a "mixed bag," and anglers were "fishing well beyond 120 feet of water." Quality 2.
- South Haven, 2023-07-05: "Salmon fishing was fair." Boats fished deep, with a few fish around 100 feet, and most fish came on spoons. Quality 1.
- Grand Haven, 2023-06-21: fair, quality 2. Fish were 35 to 90 feet down in 65 to 160 feet of water, and orange spoons and meat rigs worked. This is about four weeks old.
- Muskegon, 2023-06-07: slow, quality 1. Chinook were 30 to 100 feet down in 70 to 180 feet of water. This is the only Muskegon boat report from the last six weeks.

**Past seasons (similar weeks with surface water near 70 F)**
- Most similar weeks were slow to below average. Quality ranged from 0 to 2.
- July 2022 Grand Haven and Muskegon reports were slow, with fish at 45 to 120 feet down in 100 to 200 feet of water, and spoons (blue and green) working best.
- July 2022 St. Joseph was below average, with some fish in 30 to 40 feet of water and others well below 100 feet.

**Conditions now**
- The buoy surface water was about 71 F at St. Joseph, 71 F at South Haven, and 68 F at Muskegon and Grand Haven, all in the week before 2023-07-18. The St. Joseph reading was flat over the week, and the others rose 2 to 4 F.
- General guidance (NY DEC): Chinook and coho prefer 52 to 58 F, so the warm surface suggests the fish are holding deep, where the water is colder.
- The tools returned no cold-layer depth model and no wind forecast for these ports, so I can't say where the cold water sits or what the wind will do this week.

## Caveats

- The newest report is from 2023-07-05, about 13 days old. The bulletins are weekly, so these ratings are a guide, not a live read.
- The Grand Haven and Muskegon ratings rest on June reports and past-season patterns, so treat them as low confidence.
- The surface temperatures are measured at offshore buoys. They don't tell you the depth of the cold water, which is what the fish follow.
- I couldn't get a wind forecast. For a small boat, check the wind before heading out, and if it's strong, the pier or river is the safer alternative.

## Sources

- St. Joseph and South Haven, 2023-07-05: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/363ad03
- Grand Haven and South Haven, 2023-06-21: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3614332
- Grand Haven and Muskegon, 2023-06-07: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/35ed629
- Past-season comparisons (July 2022): https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/321350c, https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/323f6bf, https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/31f444a
